title: goal microexperiment diary - leah
content:
Goal microexperiment diary (scratchpad) - notes to self, messy thoughts, quick math

Context:
- Trying a 6-week microexperiment to move one personal metric that actually impacts team output: 'time to unblock on model-serving integration' (my proxy personal KPI).
- Hypothesis: daily 20-min focused pairing sessions + a lightweight checklist will reduce average unblock time from ~4.2 hours to <2.5 hours for the tasks I own.

Experiment design (sketch):
- Weeks 1-2: metric baseline + setup pairing slots M/W/F 9:30-9:50 (20m). Track outcomes in this doc.
- Weeks 3-4: introduce a 1-page unblock checklist (below) and a shared tiny kanban board for quick context.
- Weeks 5-6: A/B days where I skip pairing to test the causal effect, and do a short retro each Friday.

Quick unblock checklist (v0.1) - to refine
- ☐ clear statement: what exactly is blocked? (error, missing creds, unknown API?)
- ☐ last working step: where did it fail? paste minimal logs
- ☐ owned next step (5–15m task) + ETA
- ☐ who to ping (name + channel) and what to ask for (be specific)
- ☐ fallback action (work on parallel task or mock)

Weekly log (brief entries):
- 2026-02-17 (Wk1): baseline sampling. 7 unblock events logged. avg time 4.3h. Pair session: 2/3 useful; dominated by context handoff overhead. Need a 1-min pre-read template.
- 2026-02-24 (Wk2): paired all three sessions. avg unblock time for paired tasks: 2.1h, for unpaired: 4.7h. Nice signal but small n. TODO: add a quick checklist before pairing.
- 2026-03-03 (Wk3): introduced checklist. Immediately helped one incident where creds rotation tripped builds — checklist flagged 'who to ping' faster. 3 unblock events: paired 2 -> 1.4h, solo 1 -> 3.9h.
- 2026-03-09 (Wk4, current): trialing kanban microboard (sheet). friction: remembering to move cards. Idea: add a 30s 'status during standup' update.

Notes / raw thoughts (messy):
- Why this matters: unblocks for me often bubble up and cost other folks waiting on infra config. If I can speed my turnarounds, net team latency goes down. Small leverage? maybe.
- Risk: time spent pairing + upkeep could exceed gains. Need to track pairs' opportunity cost (quick estimate: 20m pairing * 3 sessions/week = 60m/week). If unblock saving < 60m/week in total, not worth it for now.
- Measurement refinement: instead of raw 'wall-clock from ticket open to resolution' (noisy), capture 'time I spend actively troubleshooting' via a quick start/stop timer (timestamp in doc). manual but higher SNR.

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Build tiny Google Sheet to log: ticket, start, stop, paired? (columns + tags). Samir volunteered to prototype viewable widget.
- [ ] Add 1-min pre-read template to pairing calendar invites (whoever pairs should drop the 3-line context).
- [ ] Run 2 A/B days Wk5 to estimate causal effect. pick Wed/Thu?
- [ ] Talk to manager (Ida) about whether to convert to weekly team practice if effect holds.

Hypothesis checklist (quick):
- Measurable? yes (time spent troubleshooting)
- Actionable? yes (pairing, checklist, kanban)
- Risky? low (time cost)
- Aligned to team? probable (faster unblocks -> faster feature delivery)

Micro-retro (end of Wk4 draft):
- What worked: pairing surfaced context faster; checklist reduced 'who to ping' latency.
- What didn't: friction on maintaining kanban; I undercounted context prep time.
- Next iteration: automate a small portion: add a calendar default description (pre-read) and make the sheet auto-create a row via a form link in the calendar invite. Samir to help with form.

Quick numbers (hand math, rough):
- baseline avg active troubleshooting per week: ~5.25 hours (7 events * ~0.75h)
- Wk2 paired sample: saved ~1.6h total across paired events vs solo baseline
- breakeven estimate (time invested in pairing to justify): 60m/week current plan -> want >60m saved = target ~1.0h/week saved beyond current. Need more weeks to see stable signal.

Links and references (for later):
- ticket examples: RED-482 (Linear) — repeated creds rotation pattern, tag 'infra-credentials'.
- convo: slack thread #infra-help 2026-02-20 (search 'creds rotation')
- proto kanban sheet: (placeholder) - I'll paste link once Samir creates it.

Random personal notes (end):
- Try to keep entries under 5 lines after each week. Easier to review in a month.
- If this shows >2h/week saved for the team, propose turning into a micro-ritual in our eng subteam cadence.

-- end scratchpad entry (will tidy into a proper OKR draft if signal holds)
